prs.title: fix: rerun setup files after `--changed` filtering
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Fixes #11586

The affected-modules walk fetched test and setup files by their file path, so the module graph kept that path as the module url and `isolate: false` workers never invalidated setup files. The walk now uses the url that workers import, and the fs module cache no longer stores the url, so caches written by 5.0.4 and 5.0.5 also recover.

prs.title: perf: reuse fsModuleCache in static collection
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Stacked on #11621.

Static collection (`experimental.preParse`, `parseSpecifications`, typecheck) transformed test files with `transformRequest`, so it never read the fs module cache and registered test files under their file path. It now uses the transform service, like the affected-modules walk.

prs.title: fix: return the mock to concurrent imports
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Fixes #7040

- Imports that start while a mock factory runs wait for it and get the same mock. Only imports made inside the factory get the original module; this is now tracked with `AsyncLocalStorage` instead of a marker on the importer's shared callstack.
- A factory that imports a module waiting for the mock gets its partial exports, like a regular import cycle, instead of hanging.
- Concurrent imports wait for mocks that `resolveMocks` is still registering.
- Concurrent imports of an automocked or spied module wait until the original module is evaluated and mocked. The second importer used to get the automock object before it was filled.

prs.title: fix: don't fail on console log pending at teardown
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Fixes #11153

Since #9727 `onUserConsoleLog` is an awaited call, so a log sent while the worker closes is rejected and reported as an unhandled error. The message is already posted at that point, so the worker now ignores the teardown rejection.

prs.title: perf(browser): map only first frame for trace locations
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- related https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/10310
- related https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11592
- notes https://gist.github.com/hi-ogawa/bc908985abae542adff13d2f3a4c132a

## Motivation

Trace view records a timeline of steps, each with its timing and source location, and takes a DOM snapshot at every step. On real app pages the snapshot is usually the larger cost. But #10310 and #11592 move toward keeping the timeline while taking snapshots only on failure, so the timeline can be shown for every failure, including in terminal output. Then the cost every passing test pays is collecting the timeline itself, and that should be cheap.

## Fix

Most of that cost was resolving each step's location. The server source-mapped every frame of the step's stack while the browser waited, although only the first usable frame is used, so the cost grew with stack depth (firefox stacks are about 40 frames per entry). This PR changes so it stops at the first frame that resolves and isn't filtered. Playwright `browser.trace` resolves action locations the same way, so it gets the same change.

## Example

One test with 200 passing `expect.element(...).toBeVisible()` calls with `traceView: true` (median of 3 runs). The page is a single button, so the snapshot cost is small and the numbers mostly show the timeline collection:

| browser | trace view off | main | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| chromium | 11ms | 544ms | 349ms |
| firefox | 21ms | 5674ms | 326ms |
| webkit | 11ms | 4
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix: reference chai types in every d.ts chunk
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Related to #11144

`vitest/runtime` types use the global `Chai` namespace but never load `@types/chai`. rollup-plugin-dts drops reference directives from `.ts` sources, so the dts build now adds `/// <reference types="chai" />` to every chunk that uses `Chai`. The new `test/e2e/dts/chai-types` fixture checks this with TypeScript 5 and 7.
